record.paper_title: Open Questions in Charm Decays Deserving an Answer
record.original_question: Do time-dependent CP asymmetries in final states common to D^0 and anti-D^0, such as K^+ K^-, pi^+ pi^-, K_S pi^0, K_S omega, and K_S eta, occur at or above the 10^-3 level once D^0-anti-D^0 oscillations are involved, which would constitute clear evidence for New Physics?

evidence.quote: Accordingly one should vigorously search for CP asymmetries involving D0−D¯ 0 oscillations: their dependance on the (proper) time of decay provides a striking experimental signature; observing them – as defined in eq.( 9) – with a size of 10−3 or above constitutes a clear sign for the intervention of NP.

Hence we arrive at the following benchmarks concerning future studies of CP violation: one should aim for achieving a 10−3 sensitivity for CP asymmetries involving D0 − D¯ 0 oscillations as well as for direct CP violation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider neutral charm mesons $D^0$ and $\bar D^0$, which mix via $\Delta C=2$ transitions parameterized by the usual mixing parameters $x=\Delta M/\Gamma$ and $y=\Delta\Gamma/(2\Gamma)$. For final states $f$ accessible to both $D^0$ and $\bar D^0$ (such as $f\in\{K^+K^-,\pi^+\pi^-,K_S\pi^0,K_S\omega,K_S\eta\}$), define the time-dependent CP asymmetry
$$A_{CP}(t;f)=\frac{\Gamma(D^0(t)\to f)-\Gamma(\bar D^0(t)\to f)}{\Gamma(D^0(t)\to f)+\Gamma(\bar D^0(t)\to f)},$$
where $D^0(t),\bar D^0(t)$ denote the time-evolved states starting as flavor eigenstates at $t=0$. The mixing-induced (oscillation-dependent) component of $A_{CP}(t;f)$ scales with $t/\tau_{D^0}$ and vanishes at $t=0$.

Determine whether the oscillation-induced contribution to the time-dependent CP asymmetry in such common final states can reach or exceed the $10^{-3}$ level within the Standard Model, or whether the observation of such an asymmetry at the $10^{-3}$ level or above would necessarily constitute clear evidence of physics beyond the Standard Model.
artifact.status_search_result: Current LHCb measurements (2021) of the time-dependent CP-asymmetry slopes $\Delta Y_{KK}=(-2.3\pm1.5\pm0.3)\times10^{-4}$ and $\Delta Y_{\pi\pi}=(-4.0\pm2.8\pm0.4)\times10^{-4}$ are consistent with CP conservation and have not yet reached or excluded the $10^{-3}$ benchmark. Standard Model predictions for mixing-induced CP asymmetries in these modes generally lie at or below $10^{-3}$, but no observation at that level has been established, so the question of whether such asymmetries exceed $10^{-3}$ (signaling New Physics) remains experimentally open.

status_evidence.title: Search for time-dependent CP violation in D0 → K+K- and D0 → π+π- decays (LHCb)
status_evidence.snippet: ΔY_{KK} = (-2.3 ± 1.5 ± 0.3) × 10^{-4} and ΔY_{ππ} = (-4.0 ± 2.8 ± 0.4) × 10^{-4}, compatible with CP conservation.
status_evidence.claim: Measurements remain at the 10^{-4} precision and have not reached the 10^{-3} threshold; no oscillation-induced CP asymmetry has been established.

status_evidence.title: PDG Review: CP Violation in the Quark Sector
status_evidence.snippet: In D meson decays CP-violating amplitudes are predicted at the 10^{-3} level in the SM, while new physics in loop diagrams may enhance effects.
status_evidence.claim: Standard Model predictions and New Physics sensitivities place the relevant benchmark near 10^{-3}; experimentally still unresolved.
